questions.stem: A patient presented with chronic sinusitis, ulcerative lesions on nasopharynx, nodular lesions with cavitation in the lungs and renal failure. What is the most important investigation?
questions.solutionHtml:
ANCA for vasculitis
  • The clinical features of the patient involving upper respiratory tract (sinusitis, ulcerative lesions on nasopharynx), lower respiratory tract (nodular lesions with cavitation in the lung) and Renal failure are suggestive of Wegener’s granulomatosis.
  • To differentiate Wagener’s granulomatosis (c – ANCA positive) from Churg Strauss syndrome (p – ANCA positive), testing for c – ANCA is necessary.

questions.stem: Not a feature of Paroxysmal Nocturnal Haemoglobinuria?
questions.solutionHtml:
Leukemia
  • Paroxysmal nocturnal Haemoglobinuria is a acquired disorder due to mutation in PIGA gene (phosphatidylinositol glycan complementation group A gene)
  • PNH cells are abnormally susceptible for lysis or injury by complement since they are deficient in three GPI linked proteins that regulate complement activity (CD55, CD59, C8 binding protein) 

Excess complement activation leads to :

  • Pancytopenia + hypercellular bone marrow
  • Intravascular Hemolysis – Hemoglobinuria
  • Thrombosis 

Diagnosis

  • Ham’s test – The abnormal sensitivity of RBCs, leukocytes and platelets to complement can be demonstrated in vitro using red cell lysis at acidic pH
  • Flow cytometry – deficiency of CD55, CD59
  • Sucrose lysis test
  • FLAER test – Fluorescein Labelled Proaerolysin test

questions.stem: Cells/mediators involved in early part of Hypersensitivity type 1 reaction are?Mast cellHistamineProstaglandinsNeutrophilsLeukotrienes Select the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
a, b, c, e

The mediators involved in early part of Type 1 hypersensitivity reaction are :

  • Mast cells
  • Histamine – Vasodilatation, Increased permeability of vessel wall, broncho constriction
  • Prostaglandins (PG D2 – Bronchoconstriction, Vasodilatation, increased vascular permeability)
  • Leukotrienes (Bronchoconstriction)
  • Enzymes like neutral proteases (chymase, tryptase) and acid hydrolases
  • Proteoglycans like heparin and chondroitin sulphate
  • Lipid mediators – platelet activation factor 

Mediator involved in late phase of type 1 hypersensitivity reaction :

  • Cytokines – TNF, IL-1, IL-4, IL-5 and Chemokines
  • Leukocytes (eosinophils)
  • Major basic protein (MBP)
  • Eosinophil cationic protein

questions.stem: Irradiation of RBCs prior to transfusion prevents which of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
Graft versus host disease
  • Graft versus host reaction (GVHD)
  • In GVHD, Immunologically active T cell of the donor destroys immunosuppressed tissues of the recipient.

GVHD is of two types

  • Acute GVHD – Occurs within days to weeks. May show rashes, jaundice, bloody diarrhoea.
  • Chronic GVHD – may follow acute GVHD or may occur insidiously. These patients have extensive skin damage, with destruction of skin appendages and fibrosis of the dermis resembling systemic sclerosis, cholestatic jaundice, esophageal strictures, involution of thymus.
  • Depletion of donor T cells by gamma irradiation, before transfusion can eliminate the occurrence of GVHD.

questions.stem: Arrange the following cellular events of inflammation in the right sequence?RollingAdhesionCytokine mediated integrin activationMigrationSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
A-C-B-D

The correct sequence of cellular events that occur during inflammation are :

  • Endothelial margination
  • Rolling
  • Cytokine mediated integrin activation
  • Adhesion
  • Leukocyte migration (Diapedesis)
  • Chemotaxis
  • Phagocytosis
  • Killing

questions.stem: Which of the following is a RNA based sequencing technique?
questions.solutionHtml:
RT-PCR
  • RT-PCR (Reverse transcriptase Polymerase Chain Reaction) is a molecular analysis method used for the detection of RNA.
  • mRNA is quantitated by generating the complementary DNA (cDNA) copies of the mRNA using reverse transcriptase enzyme.

Naive B cells

The cell of origin of CLL/SLL (Chronic lymphocytic leukemia and Small lymphocytic lymphoma) is Naive B cell.

  • The CLL and SLL differ only in the degree of peripheral blood lymphocytes
  • The most common genetic abnormalities seen are deletions of 13q14.3, 11q and 17p and trisomy 12q
  • The growth of CLL/SLL is confined to the proliferation centers
  • The tumor cells express CD19, CD20, CD23 and CD5
  • Richter’s transformation – CLL/SLL has a tendency to transform to a more aggressive DLBCL (Diffuse large B cell lymphoma)

questions.stemHtml: A 20 years old athlete suddenly collapsed while playing football and died. His case was diagnosed as a Sudden cardiac death. Based on the autopsy image shown below, what is the possible underlying cause?

options.label: A
options.text: Sudden cardiac death due to Arrythmia

options.label: B
options.text: Valvular heart disease due to RHD

options.label: C
options.text: Sudden cardiac death due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

options.label: D
options.text: Sudden cardiac death due to Atherosclerosis

questions.answerText: Sudden cardiac death due to Arrythmia
questions.solutionHtml:
Sudden cardiac death due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
  • The sudden cardiac death in the athlete and the image showing asymmetrical septal hypertrophy is suggestive of sudden cardiac death due to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
  • Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HOCM) is one of the most common cause of sudden, otherwise unexplained death in young athletes.

Features:

  • Diastolic dysfunction due to massive hypertrophy of left ventricle
  • Dynamic obstruction of left ventricular outflow as the anterior mitral leaflet moves towards the ventricular septum during systole

May lead to:

  • Atrial fibrillation
  • Stroke
  • Intractable cardiac failure
  • Ventricular arrhythmias
  • Sudden death

Mutations causing HOCM:

  • β – myosin heavy chain (MHC/MYH7)
  • Myosin binding protein C (MYBP – C)

Histology:

  • Massive myocyte hypertrophy
  • Myofiber disarray
  • Interstitial and replacement fibrosis

Management:

  • β blockers
  • Implantable cardioverter – defibrillator

questions.stem: Best method to assess Hba 1c levels?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ion chromatography
  • HbA1C is the glycated hemoglobin. It measures the mean glucose concentration over the past 6 to 8 weeks.
  • Measurement of HbA1C is done by ion exchange chromatography. 

Ion exchange chromatography

  • It is based on the charge – charge interactions
  • Two types – Cation exchange chromatography and anion exchange chromatography
  • Cation exchange – Proteins with net positive charge at a given pH will tightly adhere to the beads with negatively charged functional groups such as carboxylates and sulfates
  • Anion exchange – Proteins with net negative charge at a given pH adhere to the beads with positively charged functional groups, typically tertiary or quaternary amines.
  • Non adherent proteins are washed away

questions.stemHtml: Electron microscopic picture of an alveolus with capillary is given below. In a patient with ARDS due to SARS – COV2, which of the following layers will be expanded?
questions.solutionHtml:
A
  • In the given image of electron microscopy of blood air barrier of lungs, the marked structures are
  1. Type 2 pneumocytes
  2. Basement membrane
  3. Type 1 pneumocytes
  4. Endothelium 
  • In ARDS in patients with COVID – 19, neutrophils damage to the endothelial (labelled as D in the image) and alveolar epithelial cells, with inflammation is the key initiating event and the basis of lung damage.
  • The side of location of the endothelial can be known by the side of location of the RBC.
  • Type II pneumocyte hyperplasia is a common finding in ARDS due to the need for regeneration of the damaged type I pneumocytes

questions.stem: A 60 years old female presented with symptoms of confusion, thirst and abdominal pain. On examination, she had pallor and thoracic spine tenderness. X ray spine showed osteolytic lesions. Investigations revealed Hb 7gm%, Calcium 13mg/dl, TLC is 400/mm³ with normal DLC, Serum creatinine 2.3mg/dl, Total protein is 9g/dl and Albumin is 2.4g/dl. What is the underlying diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Multiple Myeloma

The given clinical features:

  • C - Hypercalcemia
  • R – Renal failure (suggested by elevated creatinine)
  • A – Anaemia
  • B – Osteolytic bone lesions
  • hypoalbuminemia with elevated total protein indicate multiple myeloma.
  • Multiple myeloma is a malignant plasma cell dyscrasia with the proliferation of single clone of plasma cells.
  • It is associated with an increased osteoclastic activity and suppressed osteoblastic activity causing punched out lesion in the bone and Hypercalcemia.

questions.stem: The effect of G6PD deficiency is/are:Decrease in NADPHDecrease in reduced glutathioneDecrease in lipid peroxidationDecreased RBC membrane damageSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
a, b are correct

G – 6 PD (Glucose – 6 – Phosphate Dehydrogenase) deficiency causes decrease in reduced glutathione and decreased NADPH and increased lipid peroxidation causing increased RBC membrane damage.

  • G – 6 PD reduces NADP to NADPH while oxidizing glucose 6 phosphate.
  • This NADPH provides the reducing equivalent for conversion of oxidized to reduced glutathione.
  • Reduced glutathione acts as a cofactor in reactions that neutralize the compounds such as H2O2

So, in G-6-PD deficiency, when exposed to oxidative stress RBC membrane is damaged leading to Hemolysis.

questions.stem: HPV produces a protein which suppresses RB gene. Which is it?
questions.solutionHtml:
E7

RB gene is a negative regulator of cell cycle at G1/S transition.

It exist in two states:

  • Hyperphosphorylated/inactive state
  • Hypophosphorylated / active state 

E7 protein of Human papilloma virus (HPV) binds with hypophosphorylated(active) RB gene and displaces the E2F transcription factor, and promotes G1/S transition and progression of cell cycle.

questions.stemHtml: In reference to the histopathology given below, what is most probable diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pemphigus vulgaris
  • The given image shows suprabasal splitting of epidermis and row of tombstone appearance suggestive of pemphigus vulgaris.
  • It occurs due to the antibodies mainly against desmoglein 3 and rarely against desmoglein 1. 

Features

  • Flaccid bullae
  • Both skin and mucosa involved
  • Oral mucosa is commonly affected, other areas of ulceration can be seen in conjunctiva, nasopharynx and larynx etc.
  • Cutaneous lesions are more common over scalp, face, neck, upper chest and back etc.

questions.stemHtml: The karyotype of an individual showed the following picture. Which of following clinical features may be seen in this patient ?
questions.solutionHtml:
Gynaecomastia and long limbs
  • The given karyotype have ‘47 XXY’ abnormality suggestive of klinefelter syndrome.
  • In Klinefelter syndrome Gynaecomastia and long limbs are seen.

Mnemonic - “K-L-I-N-E-F-E-L-T-S”

  • Karyotype - 47XXY
  • Long stature and long legs
  • Infertility (Incidence : 1 in 1000 men)
  • Non dysjunction of paternal sex chromosomes
  • Eunuchoid body proportions
  • FSH levels elevated, Scanty Facial and axillary hair
  • Estradiol/Testosterone ratio is elevated
  • LH elevated, Leukemias (increased risk of AML) and breast tumors, Learning disabilities
  • Testosterone reduced, small testis and penis
  • Secondary sexual characters absent

questions.stemHtml: The given below is the histological image of pancreas. Which of the marked structure is affected in cystic fibrosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
C
  • In the given image, the structures marked are:
  • A – Pancreatic duct
  • B – Blood vessels
  • C – Exocrine pancreas
  • D – Islets of Langerhans
  • In cystic fibrosis, the Exocrine pancreas will be affected (marked by ‘C' in the given image).
  • In cystic fibrosis, the CFTR protein defect leads to abnormal production of thick, sticky mucus.
  • This mucus can block the ducts of the exocrine pancreas, preventing the normal flow of digestive enzymes into the small intestine.
  • As a result, individuals with cystic fibrosis often experience pancreatic insufficiency.
